\section*{Glossary}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Glossary}
{\small\singlespacing
\begin{description}
\item[Offered task] A generated task remains in the primary outcome population whether it is admitted or rejected. [Section~\ref{sec:2.4}]
\item[Admission] Admission accepts an eligible task into a queue and is distinct from meeting its deadline. [Section~\ref{sec:2.4}]
\item[Backlog gate] The strict gate compares existing effective service workload with the candidate deadline, excluding its own service and transmission time. [Section~\ref{sec:2.4}]
\item[Task-count capacity] The queue limit constrains the number of tasks and does not increase computing service. [Section~\ref{sec:2.4}]
\item[Ingress RSU and ingress execution] Ingress is the strongest-link roadside entry point, and ingress execution keeps the task at that server. [Section~\ref{sec:2.2}]
\item[Common-target placement] One least-workload destination is selected per substep and shared by its V2I candidates. [Section~\ref{sec:2.5}]
\item[Causal per-task placement] Each candidate selects a destination using workload that immediately includes earlier admitted reservations. [Section~\ref{sec:2.5}]
\item[Causal round-robin] The cyclic comparator spreads candidates while retaining causal admission and immediate reservation. [Section~\ref{sec:2.8}]
\item[Two-choice (\texttt{dla\_p2c})] The gate-enabled alternative selects the lower-workload destination from two random candidates per vehicle. [Section~\ref{sec:2.5}]
\item[Substep] An internal task slot orders admissions within a batch without advancing the simulation clock. [Section~\ref{sec:2.4}]
\item[Drain] After the final substep, queued service work is reduced by the batch service allowance. [Section~\ref{sec:2.4}]
\item[Fleet draw and fleet seed] The fleet seed selects the draw of vehicle tier, electric-vehicle status and initial state of charge. [Section~\ref{sec:3.4}]
\item[Evaluator seed] This seed varies observations, arrivals, task types and sizes, fading and service wobble. [Section~\ref{sec:3.4}]
\item[Joint block] A paired fleet/evaluator-seed block supplies matched runs across the compared policies. [Section~\ref{sec:2.6}]
\item[Cell] A cell is a full evaluator run for one policy under its specified seed block. [Section~\ref{sec:3.4}]
\item[Sealed protocol] Controls and analysis are fixed before the full study outcomes are observed. [Section~\ref{sec:2.6}]
\item[Receipt] A validation record binds a completed run to its source, seeds and outputs. [Section~\ref{sec:3.7}]
\item[Percentage point (pp)] Paired differences subtract one policy's attainment percentage from another's on the same draw. [Section~\ref{sec:2.6}]
\item[Attainment] Offered-task deadline attainment is the share of all offered tasks recorded as meeting their deadlines. [Section~\ref{sec:2.4}]
\end{description}
}

Within the studied evaluator and matched populations, implementation semantics reverse the ingress comparison, and workload-aware causal placement improves attainment over the tested spreading rule.

% BEGIN SOURCE BLOCK 184 paragraph
Under a frozen vehicle policy, common-target placement underperformed ingress while causal per-task placement exceeded it across incident, morning and joint-randomness studies. This controlled implementation comparison demonstrates the importance of destination timing and reservation visibility within established scheduling ideas.
operations.new:
This project set out to test how infrastructure scheduling affects whether vehicle tasks meet their deadlines. This matters because useful results must arrive in time. I built and checked a frozen-actor evaluator comparison and infrastructure policies, and ran 274 full evaluator runs. In the sealed confirmation, choosing a server for each task improved deadline attainment by +4.137 percentage points over execution at the entry server and by +0.631 over cyclic spreading (Table~\ref{tab:7}). These findings remain bounded to one evaluator and one network.
% END SOURCE BLOCK 183

% BEGIN SOURCE BLOCK 184 paragraph

\textbf{Results.} All 32 full morning cells and eight block-control receipts passed after bounded qualification, with no failed attempts, retries or exclusions. Table~\ref{tab:7} reports the declared contrasts; Appendix~\ref{app:E} retains every block \hyperref[source-s16]{[S16]}.

\textbf{Setting.} Evaluator seed varies observation descriptors, arrivals, operational types/sizes, fading and service wobble; fleet seed varies tier, EV status and initial SoC. The estimand remains the total scheduling intervention under frozen weights, without forcing replay or guaranteeing future action equality. Small observation and logit differences occurred in block 1; they did not change actions. All four arms shared the required exogenous arrays exactly within each block, and actions matched exactly in all 24 non-reference arm/block comparisons.

operations.old: The findings support a bounded benefit from workload awareness beyond spreading. Two checkpoints sharing one training seed, one calibrated Manchester network for all five scenarios, global service-work information and aggregate timing restrict generalisation and physical interpretation. Historical capacity findings separately retain inconclusive statistics and unresolved scoring uncertainty; the later gate-enabled results do not resolve that gap.

Two checkpoints sharing one training seed, one demand-scaled Manchester network for all five scenarios, global service-work information and aggregate timing restrict generalisation and physical interpretation. Historical capacity findings separately retain inconclusive statistics and unresolved scoring uncertainty; the later gate-enabled results do not resolve that gap.

operations.old: Both traces are exported from the calibrated Manchester SUMO network of Putra et al., built from OpenStreetMap around the Etihad Stadium and Co-op Live with demand generated from Transport for Greater Manchester sensor counts; the incident hour is that study's documented reactive-control collapse on 15 March 2024, used here as a simulated dense-traffic stress case rather than a recorded incident \cite{ref47}.
operations.new: Both traces use Putra et al.'s count-matched, demand-scaled Manchester SUMO network around Etihad Stadium and Co-op Live \cite{ref47}. The source study builds the network from OpenStreetMap, scales demand uniformly to 70\% of observed sensor counts to avoid simulated gridlock, and reports SUMO 1.27.0 \cite{ref47}. The incident hour is that study's documented reactive-control collapse on 15 March 2024, used here as a simulated dense-traffic stress case rather than a recorded incident.

count_source_overrides.13: The Manchester scenarios, taken from a count-matched, demand-scaled Manchester SUMO network around Etihad and Co-op Live [[47]](#ref-47), give the comparison a concrete intelligent-transport setting. I use saved SUMO working-day and incident-model traces as repeatable inputs, exposing the same scheduling rules to different scenario conditions. These simulated movements do not establish live performance on Manchester roads. An operator must decide whether to retain ingress execution, distribute work or alter admission, accounting for coordination cost and available service.

count_source_overrides.152: **Recurrence on three further Manchester traces.** A further declared study ran the same five arms on eight seed blocks for each of three traces not previously used in this dissertation, from the same demand-scaled network: weekend (Sunday 15 September 2024, 12:00–21:00), weekday evening peak (Tuesday 15 October 2024, 14:00–21:00) and event night (Wednesday 18 September 2024, 17:30–24:00), 120 cells with no failures, protocol sealed before outcomes (Table 7b). The ranking common-target < ingress < round-robin < per-task recurred on every trace: common-target lost 3.0 to 3.6 points to ingress, per-task gained 3.7 to 4.4, and per-task exceeded round-robin by +0.43 to +0.61 and two-choice by +0.53 to +0.65, with all fifteen intervals adjusted as one family. In trace means, two-choice never exceeded round-robin and trailed it on the weekend and event traces. Descriptively, ordered by mean active vehicles per second, the workload-aware increment rose monotonically across event night, weekend, evening peak and morning (0.43, 0.51, 0.61, 0.63), consistent with the half-speed result; event night also has twelve RSUs against nine or ten. The weekend trace carries the entry-channel fix; the evening-peak and event traces retain the legacy slot-reuse convention noted for the incident trace [[S19]](#source-s19).

count_source_overrides.194: RQ3 is limited to the completed models. The 100 ms reports equalled fresh state; older-report changes were small under live admission and reservations. A single-draw fixed-overhead calculation retained per-task's advantage over ingress through 10 ms without modelling congestion or feedback. count_source_overrides.61: The initial two scenarios are drawn from the Manchester SUMO working-day and incident models: `manchester_workingday/trace_wd_am_wdrsu.npz` and the 15 March 2024 incident trace (Table 2). Both traces use Putra et al.'s count-matched, demand-scaled Manchester SUMO network around Etihad Stadium and Co-op Live [[47]](#ref-47). The source study builds the network from OpenStreetMap, scales demand uniformly to 70% of observed sensor counts to avoid simulated gridlock, and reports SUMO 1.27.0 [[47]](#ref-47). The incident hour is that study's documented reactive-control collapse on 15 March 2024, used here as a simulated dense-traffic stress case rather than a recorded incident. Coordinates are local trace metres. Evaluations import saved positions without rerunning SUMO. Morning input checks reconstruct canonical arrays and verify entry markers because padded slots need not retain one vehicle identity. Queues reset for each new visit; SoC does not. The incident trace retains its earlier convention without the same entry channel [[S7]](#source-s7).
count_source_overrides.142: **Setting.** Evaluator seed varies observation descriptors, arrivals, operational types/sizes, fading and service wobble; fleet seed varies tier, EV status and initial SoC. The estimand remains the total scheduling intervention under frozen weights, without forcing replay or guaranteeing future action equality. Small observation and logit differences occurred in block 1; they did not change actions. All four arms shared the required exogenous arrays exactly within each block, and actions matched exactly in all 24 non-reference arm/block comparisons.
count_source_overrides.143: **Results.** All 32 full morning cells and eight block-control receipts passed after bounded qualification, with no failed attempts, retries or exclusions. Table 7 reports the declared contrasts; Appendix E retains every block [[S16]](#source-s16).
count_source_overrides.183: This project set out to test how infrastructure scheduling affects whether vehicle tasks meet their deadlines. This matters because useful results must arrive in time. I built and checked a frozen-actor evaluator comparison and infrastructure policies, and ran 274 full evaluator runs. In the sealed confirmation, choosing a server for each task improved deadline attainment by +4.137 percentage points over execution at the entry server and by +0.631 over cyclic spreading (Table 7). These findings remain bounded to one evaluator and one network.
